title: “In the thirtieth year” — counted from what?
summary: Ezekiel 1:1 dates the vision “in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month”. The verse does not say what the thirtieth year is counted from.
text: KJV Ezekiel 1:1: “Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month, as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.” KJV Ezekiel 1:2: “In the fifth day of the month, which was the fifth year of king Jehoiachin's captivity,”
reasoning: The next verse gives a second date, “the fifth year of king Jehoiachin’s captivity”, and names the day of the month again. Verse 1 gives “the thirtieth year” without a king, an event or an era. Possible readings, named only as readings: the thirtieth year of the prophet’s own age; a count of years from an earlier event in the nation’s history; a count of years belonging to another reckoning than the captivity of verse 2. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the two verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not claim that no other passage says more about the date.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: Now it came to pass in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, in the fifth day of the month

title: “The years of their iniquity … three hundred and ninety days” — which years?
summary: Ezekiel 4:5 says the days laid on the prophet are “the years of their iniquity”, three hundred and ninety, and 4:6 adds forty for Judah. The verses do not say when those years begin or which years they are.
text: KJV Ezekiel 4:4: “Lie thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it: according to the number of the days that thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquity.” KJV Ezekiel 4:5: “For I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days: so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.” KJV Ezekiel 4:6: “And when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side, and thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.”
reasoning: The days are set against “the years of their iniquity” and “each day for a year”. The verses give the numbers, three hundred and ninety for “the house of Israel” and forty for “the house of Judah”, but no starting point, no event that ends the count and no list of the years. Possible readings, named only as readings: a stretch of past years of the nation’s guilt; a stretch of years of coming punishment; a figure given for its meaning and not as a count. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the three verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one and does not claim that no other passage says more about the years. It does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek (the Greek number at 4:5 is the subject of a separate record).

sides.label: A
sides.quote: the years of their iniquity, according to the number of the days, three hundred and ninety days

title: “I the Lord have deceived that prophet” — how, and why is he then destroyed?
summary: Ezekiel 14:9 says that if a prophet “be deceived” the Lord has “deceived that prophet”, and will destroy him. The verses do not say how the deceiving is done.
text: KJV Ezekiel 14:4: “Therefore speak unto them, and say unto them, Thus saith the Lord God; Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart, and putteth the stumblingblock of his iniquity before his face, and cometh to the prophet; I the Lord will answer him that cometh according to the multitude of his idols;” KJV Ezekiel 14:9: “And if the prophet be deceived when he hath spoken a thing, I the Lord have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand upon him, and will destroy him from the midst of my people Israel.” KJV Ezekiel 14:10: “And they shall bear the punishment of their iniquity: the punishment of the prophet shall be even as the punishment of him that seeketh unto him;”
reasoning: Verse 4 says the Lord will answer the idolater “according to the multitude of his idols”. Verse 9 says the Lord has deceived the prophet and will destroy him, and verse 10 says the prophet and the one who seeks him bear a like punishment. The verses do not say by what means the prophet is deceived, or whether he is deceived before or after his own wrong. Possible readings, named only as readings: a judgment that gives a hearer the answer he wants; a permitting of a false answer; a sending of a false message. The record does not decide between them.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The question is limited to the three verses quoted. The record does not say that any reading is the right one, does not rest on the Hebrew or the Greek, and does not claim that no other passage says more about the deceiving.

sides.label: A
sides.quote: I the Lord have deceived that prophet
